mathcounts-potw-2025-11-24-01.title: Favorable seats over all seats
mathcounts-potw-2025-11-24-01.body:
Since Grady can't read, Uncle Rob's card is equally likely to land at any of the 8 settings. Two of them are on the short sides, so the probability is $\frac{2}{8} = \frac14$.

**Answer: $\frac14$**

mathcounts-potw-2025-11-24-01.title: Complement
mathcounts-potw-2025-11-24-01.body:
The chance his card is on a long side is $\frac{6}{8} = \frac34$, so the chance it is on a short side is $1 - \frac34 = \frac14$.

**Answer: $\frac14$**

mathcounts-potw-2025-11-24-02.title: Yes/no for each side dish
mathcounts-potw-2025-11-24-02.body:
Turkey is always taken. Each of the 5 side dishes is either taken or not, so there are $2^5 = 32$ combinations (including turkey alone).

**Answer: 32**

mathcounts-potw-2025-11-24-02.title: Count by number of side dishes

mathcounts-potw-2025-11-24-03.title: Angle of the eaten part
mathcounts-potw-2025-11-24-03.body:
The 8 slices make up $1 - \frac13 = \frac23$ of the pie, which is $\frac23 \times 360° = 240°$. Each slice: $240° \div 8 = 30°$.

**Answer: 30 degrees**

mathcounts-potw-2025-11-24-03.title: Fraction per slice
mathcounts-potw-2025-11-24-03.body:
Each slice is $\frac23 \div 8 = \frac{1}{12}$ of the pie, and $\frac{1}{12}$ of $360°$ is $30°$.

**Answer: 30 degrees**
